correctness.rationale: Reconstructed Definition 4.1 exactly. Edge addition makes A_t={B_a p worlds} decrease. If consecutive A sets agree and nonempty, every agent/world row meets A after the update, so a further update is inert; this gives at most n strict steps. While A meets the false-p set, surviving A-rows have their original successors, so they survive iff they have an edge into A: the outgoing-sink recursion. The directed path with p false only at the source yields n strict steps, including n=1. Propositional truth sets do not change, giving one-step idempotence. The saved standalone checker gives 4,164 exhaustive and 50,000 sampled one-agent cases, 1,032 exhaustive and 30,000 sampled multi-agent cases, 4,164 propositional tests and 29 sharp-path checks. Finite checks do not replace the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 source explicitly motivates studying iteration and defines a dynamics that can repeatedly change its own modal counterexamples. The new result gives an exact structural procedure (outgoing-sink peeling), a sharp uniform world-count bound valid for any number of agents, and a minimally modal one-atom family attaining every horizon. This separates modal depth zero from one and rules out the plausible assumption that adding every available counterexample at once makes repetition redundant. Its consequence is a complete finite-horizon answer for a natural fixed HPAL update, not an arbitrary census slice.
